newsitem.title: SPAIN: Madrid stocks firm but short-term trend unclear.
newsitem.headline: Madrid stocks firm but short-term trend unclear.

text.p: Madrid stocks firmed in line with bonds on Tuesday, but only a small group of key shares benefited, creating uncertainty about the bourse's short-term direction.
The general index up 1.83 points, 0.50 percent, to 370.10, while the Ibex-35 leading share index rose 24.14 points, 0.57 percent, to 4,239.71.
Repsol was a key gainer, up 95 pesetas, 2.25 percent, to 4,315 with 720,411 shares traded. Traders said the rise had more to do with technical factors than any fundamental reasons.
"The market remains firm with the chance of rising further in view of debt levels, with money going towards key shares," said a trader.
The market was eyeing the Bank of Spain's repo tender on Thursday at which it expects the key money market rate to be cut between 25 and 50 basis points from 7.25 percent.
Traders said it was difficult to see a clear short-term direction as sectors sharply varied in their performance.

Telefonica was up 20 pesetas to 2,405 with 3.5 million shares exchanging hands. Most large banks posted gains inferior to 0.6 percent, while among electricity firms Endesa lost 10 pesetas to 7,550 and Iberdrola rose 15 to 1,260.
